gen-dafont-quantum-gf-krub: Krub reads with a tall, friendly lowercase and curves that never quite close. Quantum is the showy one, stencil-cut letters all at a single width, while the sans-serif below simply does the quiet work of being easy on the eye.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-kufam: Clean from top to bottom, with Kufam's open-bellied e and its tall bodies crowding out the ascenders below Quantum's heading. Quantum does the loud, spaced-out display work; the sans just keeps the lines moving.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-lexend: Wide, open and a bit oversized. Quantum gives headings a spaced-out, techy look, while Lexend's plain sans lowercase keeps every curve gaping and every stroke the same thickness around the bend.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-lexend-deca: Lexend Deca draws a plain line that never swells, with small capitals beside big lowercase. Its simple, unshaded shapes are the pair's strongest quality, and Quantum's spaced-out display letters sit above them without any fuss.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-liter: Tall and unfussy, with Liter's sans lowercase standing up straight and no stroke contrast at all. And Quantum above it loosens the spacing for a techy heading, so a modest size jump between the two is plenty.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-mada: Straight lines up top, open curves below. And the strongest quality here is Mada's towering midzone, which stands against Quantum's heading, where vertical and horizontal strokes carry identical weight.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-martel-sans: Modern in feel, with Quantum drawing glass-tube lettering that stays hollow and constant in thickness. Martel Sans follows in sans-serif form, its curves generously open and a high mean line running across every word.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-maven-pro: Loose, generous spacing marks Quantum's display letters, each with mouths that stay wide open. And Maven Pro, a sans-serif with a gentle monotone line and a high-waisted lowercase, is the quiet strength of the pair.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-michroma: Wide-set and techy, with Quantum's rope-thin outline running across the heading. Michroma then gives each letter a wide berth, a tall-bodied sans lowercase with stubby ascender tips that keeps the page open.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-miriam-libre: Miriam Libre reads like drawn wire, with a lowercase as tall as cast iron capitals. Quantum handles the spaced-out, techy display work, while Miriam Libre's sans-serif curves, an s with open bends, do the steadier job.
